title_en: Regulations on Scenic and Historic Areas

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated for the purpose of strengthening the administration of scenic and historic areas, effectively protecting and rationally utilizing scenic and historic resources.

Article 2 The establishment, planning, protection, utilization and administration of scenic and historic areas shall be governed by these Regulations.
For the purposes of these Regulations, "scenic and historic area" means an area which has scenic, cultural or scientific value, where natural and cultural landscapes are comparatively concentrated, the environment is beautiful, and which is available for people to visit or to conduct scientific and cultural activities.
Article 3 The State shall apply the principles of scientific planning, unified administration, strict protection and sustainable utilization in respect of scenic and historic areas.

Article 4 The administrative body for scenic and historic areas established by the local people's government at or above the county level in the locality of a scenic and historic area shall be responsible for the protection, utilization and unified administration of the scenic and historic area.

Article 5 The administrative department of construction under the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of scenic and historic areas nationwide. Other relevant departments under the State Council shall, in accordance with the division of responsibilities prescribed by the State Council, be responsible for the relevant supervision and administration of scenic and historic areas.
The administrative departments of construction of the people's governments of provinces and autonomous regions and the competent departments of scenic and historic areas of the people's governments of municipalities directly under the Central Government shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of scenic and historic areas within their respective administrative regions. Other relevant departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, in accordance with the prescribed division of responsibilities, be responsible for the relevant supervision and administration of scenic and historic areas.
Article 6 All entities and individuals shall have the duty to protect scenic and historic resources, and shall have the right to stop and report any acts that damage scenic and historic resources.

Article 7 The establishment of a scenic and historic area shall be conducive to the protection and rational utilization of scenic and historic resources.
A newly established scenic and historic area shall not overlap or intersect with any nature reserve; where an established scenic and historic area overlaps or intersects with a nature reserve, the plan for the scenic and historic area and the plan for the nature reserve shall be coordinated.

Article 8 Scenic and historic areas are classified into national scenic and historic areas and provincial scenic and historic areas.
An area whose natural and cultural landscapes reflect important natural change processes and major historical and cultural development processes, are basically in a natural state or maintain their original historical appearance, and are of national representativeness, may apply for establishment as a national scenic and historic area; an area with regional representativeness may apply for establishment as a provincial scenic and historic area.

Article 10 For the establishment of a national scenic and historic area, the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government shall submit an application; the administrative department of construction under the State Council shall, in conjunction with the environmental protection department, forestry department, cultural relics department and other relevant departments under the State Council, organize a demonstration, put forward examination opinions, and submit the same to the State Council for approval and promulgation.
For the establishment of a provincial scenic and historic area, the people's government of the county shall submit an application; the administrative department of construction of the people's government of the province or autonomous region, or the competent department of scenic and historic areas of the people's government of the municipality directly under the Central Government, shall, in conjunction with other relevant departments, organize a demonstration, put forward examination opinions, and submit the same to the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government for approval and promulgation.

Article 11 The lawful rights and interests of the owners and right holders of the land, forests and other natural resources as well as houses and other property within a scenic and historic area shall be protected by law.
The people's government applying for the establishment of a scenic and historic area shall, before submitting the application for examination and approval, fully consult with the owners and right holders of the land, forests and other natural resources as well as houses and other property within the scenic and historic area.
Where losses are caused to the owners and right holders of the land, forests and other natural resources as well as houses and other property within a scenic and historic area due to the establishment thereof, compensation shall be made according to law.
Article 12 Plans for scenic and historic areas are classified into master plans and detailed plans.
Article 14 A master plan for a scenic and historic area shall be completed within two years from the date of its establishment. The planning period of a master plan shall generally be 20 years.

Article 15 Detailed plans for a scenic and historic area shall be prepared according to the different requirements of core scenic spots and other scenic spots, determine the site selection, layout and scale of construction projects such as infrastructure, tourism facilities and cultural facilities, and specify the scope of land for construction and planning and design conditions.
Detailed plans for a scenic and historic area shall conform to the master plan for the scenic and historic area.

Article 16 The plan for a national scenic and historic area shall be organized and prepared by the administrative department of construction of the people's government of the province or autonomous region, or the competent department of scenic and historic areas of the people's government of the municipality directly under the Central Government.
The plan for a provincial scenic and historic area shall be organized and prepared by the people's government of the county.

Article 17 In preparing a plan for a scenic and historic area, the unit to undertake the task shall be selected through fair competition such as public bidding and shall have corresponding qualification grades.
The plan for a scenic and historic area shall be prepared in accordance with the approved scope, nature and protection objectives of the scenic and historic area, and in accordance with the relevant State laws, regulations and technical standards.

Article 18 In preparing a plan for a scenic and historic area, opinions of relevant departments, the public and experts shall be extensively solicited; where necessary, a hearing shall be held.
The materials submitted for examination and approval of a plan for a scenic and historic area shall include opinions from all sectors of society, the status of adoption of such opinions, and the reasons for not adopting them.

Article 19 The master plan for a national scenic and historic area shall be subject to review by the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government, and then submitted to the State Council for approval.
The detailed plan for a national scenic and historic area shall be submitted by the administrative department of construction of the people's government of the province or autonomous region, or the competent department of scenic and historic areas of the people's government of the municipality directly under the Central Government, to the administrative department of construction under the State Council for approval.

Article 20 The master plan for a provincial scenic and historic area shall be subject to approval by the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government, and shall be filed with the administrative department of construction under the State Council for record.
The detailed plan for a provincial scenic and historic area shall be subject to approval by the administrative department of construction of the people's government of the province or autonomous region, or the competent department of scenic and historic areas of the people's government of the municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 21 After a plan for a scenic and historic area is approved, it shall be published to the public, and any organization or individual shall have the right to consult it.
Entities and individuals within the scenic and historic area shall comply with the approved plan for the scenic and historic area and submit to the planning administration.
Where a plan for a scenic and historic area has not been approved, no construction activities of any kind shall be carried out within the scenic and historic area.

Article 22 An approved plan for a scenic and historic area shall not be modified without authorization. Where it is truly necessary to modify the scope, nature, protection objectives, ecological resource protection measures, layout of major construction projects, intensity of development and utilization, as well as functional structure, spatial layout or visitor capacity of the scenic and historic area in the master plan, the matter shall be submitted to the original approving authority for approval; where other contents need to be modified, the matter shall be submitted to the original approving authority for record.
Where it is truly necessary to modify a detailed plan for a scenic and historic area, the matter shall be submitted to the original approving authority for approval.
Where the government or a government department modifies a plan for a scenic and historic area, causing property losses to citizens, legal persons or other organizations, compensation shall be made according to law.

Article 23 Two years before the expiration of the planning period of the master plan for a scenic and historic area, the authority that organized the preparation of the plan shall organize experts to evaluate the plan and make a decision on whether to re-prepare the plan. Before the new plan is approved, the original plan shall remain valid.

Article 24 The landscapes and natural environment within a scenic and historic area shall be strictly protected in accordance with the principle of sustainable development, and shall not be damaged or altered arbitrarily.
The administrative body for the scenic and historic area shall establish and improve various management systems for the protection of scenic and historic resources.
Residents and visitors within the scenic and historic area shall protect the scenic features, water bodies, forest and grass vegetation, wild animals and various facilities of the scenic and historic area.

Article 25 The administrative body for a scenic and historic area shall investigate and evaluate the important landscapes within the scenic and historic area, and formulate corresponding protection measures.

Article 27 It is prohibited to establish various development zones within a scenic and historic area in violation of the plan for the scenic and historic area, and to build hotels, guesthouses, training centers, sanatoria and other buildings unrelated to the protection of scenic and historic resources within the core scenic spots; those already built shall be gradually relocated in accordance with the plan for the scenic and historic area.

Article 28 Where construction activities beyond the scope prohibited in Articles 26 and 27 of these Regulations are engaged in within a scenic and historic area, the matter shall be subject to examination by the administrative body for the scenic and historic area, and then the formalities for examination and approval shall be gone through in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and regulations.
Where major construction projects such as cable cars and ropeways are built within a national scenic and historic area, the site selection plan for the project shall be submitted to the administrative department of construction of the people's government of the province or autonomous region, or the competent department of scenic and historic areas of the people's government of the municipality directly under the Central Government, for verification and approval.

Article 30 Construction projects within a scenic and historic area shall conform to the plan for the scenic and historic area and be in harmony with the landscape, and shall not damage the landscape, pollute the environment or impede touring.
Where construction activities are carried out within a scenic and historic area, the construction entity and the construction unit shall formulate plans for pollution prevention and soil and water conservation, and take effective measures to protect the surrounding scenic features, water bodies, forest and grass vegetation, wildlife resources and landforms.

Article 31 The State shall establish a management information system for scenic and historic areas to conduct dynamic monitoring of the implementation of plans for scenic and historic areas and the protection of resources.
The administrative body for a national scenic and historic area in the locality thereof shall, each year, submit to the administrative department of construction under the State Council a report on the implementation of the plan for the scenic and historic area and the protection of natural resources such as land and forests; the administrative department of construction under the State Council shall promptly send a copy of the report on the protection of natural resources such as land and forests to the relevant departments under the State Council.

Article 32 The administrative body for a scenic and historic area shall, in light of the characteristics of the scenic and historic area, protect the traditional cultures of ethnic groups and folk customs, conduct healthy and beneficial sightseeing and cultural entertainment activities, and popularize historical, cultural and scientific knowledge.

Article 33 The administrative body for a scenic and historic area shall, in accordance with the plan for the scenic and historic area, rationally utilize the scenic and historic resources and improve transportation, service facilities and touring conditions.
The administrative body for a scenic and historic area shall set up signs for the scenic and historic area, as well as road signs, safety warning signs and other signage within the scenic and historic area.

Article 34 The administration of religious activity sites within a scenic and historic area shall be carried out in accordance with the State provisions on the administration of religious activity sites.
Where matters within a scenic and historic area involve the protection, utilization and administration of natural resources, the protection of cultural relics, and the administration of nature reserves, the relevant State laws and regulations shall also be implemented.

Article 35 The administrative department of construction under the State Council shall conduct supervision, inspection and evaluation of the implementation of plans and the status of resource protection of national scenic and historic areas. Problems discovered shall be promptly corrected and dealt with.

Article 36 The administrative body for a scenic and historic area shall establish and improve a safety guarantee system, strengthen safety management, ensure touring safety, and urge business units within the scenic and historic area to accept supervision and inspection conducted by relevant departments in accordance with laws and regulations.
It is prohibited to admit visitors beyond the permitted capacity or to conduct touring activities in areas without safety guarantees.

Article 37 Tickets for entering a scenic and historic area shall be sold by the administrative body for the scenic and historic area. The ticket prices shall be determined in accordance with the laws and regulations on prices.
For transportation, service and other projects within a scenic and historic area, the operator shall be determined by the administrative body for the scenic and historic area through fair competition such as public bidding in accordance with relevant laws, regulations and the plan for the scenic and historic area.
The administrative body for the scenic and historic area shall enter into a contract with the operator and determine their respective rights and obligations according to law. The operator shall pay a fee for the compensated use of the scenic and historic resources.

Article 38 The ticketing revenue and the fees for compensated use of scenic and historic resources shall be managed under a system of separate revenue and expenditure.
The ticketing revenue and the fees for compensated use of scenic and historic resources shall be used exclusively for the protection and administration of scenic and historic resources and for compensating the losses of the owners and right holders of property within the scenic and historic area. The specific measures for administration shall be formulated by the finance department and the price department under the State Council, in conjunction with the administrative department of construction under the State Council and other relevant departments.

Article 39 The administrative body for a scenic and historic area shall not engage in for-profit business activities, and shall not entrust the administrative functions such as planning, management and supervision to any enterprise or individual.
The staff of the administrative body for a scenic and historic area shall not hold any concurrent position in any enterprise within the scenic and historic area.

Article 40 Where any of the following acts is committed in violation of these Regulations, the administrative body for the scenic and historic area shall order the cessation of the illegal act, restoration to the original condition or demolition within a time limit, confiscate the illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan:
(1) engaging in activities such as quarrying, mining, opening hillsides that damage landscapes, vegetation and landforms within a scenic and historic area;
(2) constructing facilities for storing explosive, inflammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive articles within a scenic and historic area; or
(3) building hotels, guesthouses, training centers, sanatoria or other buildings unrelated to the protection of scenic and historic resources within core scenic spots.
Where a local people's government at or above the county level or its relevant competent department approves the carrying out of an act specified in the preceding paragraph, the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given a demotion or dismissal according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 41 Where, in violation of these Regulations, construction activities beyond the prohibited scope are engaged in within a scenic and historic area without examination by the administrative body for the scenic and historic area, the administrative body for the scenic and historic area shall order the cessation of construction and demolition within a time limit, and impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan on an individual, and a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan on an entity.

Article 42 Where, in violation of these Regulations, a major construction project such as a cable car or ropeway is built within a national scenic and historic area, and the site selection plan for the project has not been verified and approved by the administrative department of construction of the people's government of the province or autonomous region, or the competent department of scenic and historic areas of the people's government of the municipality directly under the Central Government, and a relevant department of a local people's government at or above the county level issues a site selection opinion letter, the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given a sanction according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 43 Where, in violation of these Regulations, an individual engages in activities such as reclaiming land, building graves or erecting monuments that damage landscapes, vegetation and landforms within a scenic and historic area, the administrative body for the scenic and historic area shall order the cessation of the illegal act, restoration to the original condition or the taking of other remedial measures within a time limit, confiscate the illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 1,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan.

Article 44 Where, in violation of these Regulations, a person inscribes or defaces on scenic features or facilities, or litters within a scenic and historic area, the administrative body for the scenic and historic area shall order restoration to the original condition or the taking of other remedial measures, and impose a fine of 50 yuan; where a person intentionally damages State-protected cultural relics or places of historic interest and scenic beauty by inscribing, defacing or other means, the person shall be punished in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Law on Public Security Administration Punishments; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 46 Where, in violation of these Regulations, a construction unit, during the construction process, causes damage to the surrounding scenic features, water bodies, forest and grass vegetation, wildlife resources and landforms, the administrative body for the scenic and historic area shall order the cessation of the illegal act, restoration to the original condition or the taking of other remedial measures within a time limit, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan; if restoration to the original condition or effective measures are not taken within the time limit, the administrative body for the scenic and historic area shall order the suspension of construction.

Article 49 Where, in respect of the illegal acts specified in the first paragraph of Article 40, Article 41, Article 43, Article 44, Article 45 and Article 46 of these Regulations, the relevant departments have already imposed punishment in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations, the administrative body for the scenic and historic area shall not impose punishment again.

Article 50 Where the illegal acts specified in the first paragraph of Article 40, Article 41, Article 43, Article 44, Article 45 and Article 46 of these Regulations infringe upon the property of the State, a collective or an individual, the relevant entity or individual shall bear civil liability according to law.

Article 51 Where an order is made in accordance with these Regulations to demolish within a time limit the buildings, structures or other facilities illegally constructed in a scenic and historic area, the relevant entity or individual shall immediately cease the construction activities and demolish them on its/his own; where construction continues, the authority that made the order for demolition within a time limit shall have the power to stop it. If the relevant entity or individual disagrees with the demolition order, it/he may file a prosecution with the People's Court within 15 days from the date of receipt of the demolition order; if no prosecution is filed within the time limit and the demolition is not carried out on its/his own, the authority that made the demolition order shall, according to law, apply to the People's Court for compulsory execution, and the expenses shall be borne by the violator.

Article 52 These Regulations shall come into force as of December 1, 2006. The Interim Regulations on the Administration of Scenic and Historic Areas promulgated by the State Council on June 7, 1985 shall be abolished simultaneously.
